name: CAPS MENTAL HEALTH GROUPS SPRING 2026
description:
Led by our licensed clinicians, our groups and support spaces help you improve your relationships, learn about yourself and others, enhance your communication skills, and reduce isolation within a supportive, normalizing environment of peers.

Group Counseling

At CAPS, we offer group therapy as a valuable opportunity for self-discovery and addressing concerns in a supportive and collaborative environment. Our group sessions typically consist of 4-10 students who meet weekly throughout the semester, all under the expert guidance of our CAPS clinicians. Joining a group allows you to gain valuable insights into yourself and others, fostering personal growth and understanding in a nurturing setting.

name: SENIOR WEEK: Last Night
description: It’s the last night, and you won’t want to miss out! This year's Last Night tradition is bigger and better: bring your friends and families to enjoy our margarita bar, arcade games, and more! Let's close out Senior Week with the best night yet!

name: CAPS Presents: The Next Phase: a Support-Focused Group for Students Who Will Soon Graduate
description: This group is for both undergraduate and graduate school students who are nearing graduation and preparing for the next chapters in their lives. It is a peer support space where students have an opportunity to share their affective and cognitive experiences regarding their futures. This mutual disclosure and exploration is intended to help normalize the students' experiences and facilitate support, encouragement and helpful reflection and feedback.

name: SENIOR WEEK: Back to the Vern
description: Former Vernies, you are invited back to the Mount Vernon Campus to reminisce and celebrate your GW journey. Join us for brunch, giveaways and a toast to the graduates!

name: SENIOR WEEK: First-Gen Senior Class Photo
description: Join us for a celebratory Senior Class Photo as we bring together the Class of 2026 to mark this important milestone. This event offers graduating seniors a chance to come together for a large group photo to commemorate their time at GW and celebrate their achievements alongside their peers. This will serve as a meaningful keepsake for students as they prepare to graduate and reflect on their journey.

name: SENIOR WEEK: First-Gen Senior Photos
description:
Celebrate your achievement as a first-generation college graduate with professional graduation portraits! Join us for the First-Gen Graduation Photos event, where graduating seniors will have the opportunity to take professional photos in their cap and gown, as well as an additional outfit of their choice. Students will be able to take one photo in their graduation attire and one in an outfit of their choice, so we encourage them to have both ready for their scheduled time slot. Each student will receive a short time slot to capture a few high-quality images to commemorate this important milestone. This is a great opportunity to celebrate your journey, represent your first-gen identity, and create lasting memories as you prepare to graduate.

Spring 2026 Sessions

March 5 | 5:00 PM — CISL, USC 240

We look forward to celebrating you and sending you off in a way that reflects your impact on our campus community.

Bring your friends, bring your appetite, and let’s make the last week before finals a little sweeter and a lot more delicious!

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: Movie Night in Georgetown: 'Michael' @AMC Georgetown 14
description:
Michael is a 2026 American musical biographical drama film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by John Logan.

It follows the life of American singer Michael Jackson, covering the period from his involvement in the Jackson 5 in the 60s to his early solo career. Jackson is portrayed by his nephew Jaafar Jackson in his film debut.

The ensemble cast includes Nia Long, Laura Harrier, Juliano Krue Valdi, Miles Teller, and Colman Domingo.

The music.

The moments.

The legacy that moved the world. In partnership with Lionsgate, BET takes you back to the performances that defined a generation—and still hit just as hard today.

From the first note to the final move, Michael Jackson didn’t just perform… he created moments we all remember.

MONDAY, April 27th 

We will be traveling to AMC Georgetown 14. 

Will be meeting in the lobby Guthridge Hall @6:30pm. 

Movie Starts @7:10pm.  Run time is 127 minutes.  

Tickets are on us. Your ride there and back in on us. 

Popcorn, Soda Pop, & Candy on you! 

First some, First serve. So RSVP Soon.

name: GW HALT Hazing - Required Training Session
description:
GW HALT Hazing is a comprehensive safety and leadership initiative designed to empower GW students. HALT adopts a dual-focus approach to hazing prevention: psychological and physical dangers of hazing while equipping students with the medical literacy to prevent alcohol-related tragedies and the skills to transform their organizations with healthy, values-based new member programs. GW HALT seeks to ensure that every Revolutionary has the knowledge to protect themselves and the courage to protect each other.

In line with Virginia’s Adam’s Law and in the spirit of promoting a shared vocabulary of safety and respect across campus, the program is mandatory for ALL current members of Student Organizations with New Members. These are defined as officially recognized organizations where individuals do not automatically become members upon invitation and must complete a "new member period" before full initiation. If an organization fails to obtain 100% compliance by the conclusion of the academic year, it will be placed on frozen status until members missing the training complete it. Visit the GW HALT Hazing webpage for more information 

You must attend the entire training to receive credit, and attendance is taken at both the beginning and end.

name: FPP's 9 to 5
location: Blackbox Theatre, B2 Level West Hall MVC
description:
Forbidden Planet Productions presents 9 to 5, directed by Devika Mukherjee, with Teresa Seraphin, Jai Gough, Lila Trout, Jacob Khabie, and Narissa AlDayaa! Set in the late 1970s, this high-energy musical follows three coworkers who band together to take control of their toxic workplace and turn the tables on their sexist boss. Packed with humor, heart, and music by Dolly Parton, it’s a story of friendship, revenge, and empowerment in a man’s world. Join us this weekend for a bold, hilarious, and feel-good night at the theater!

 

📅 April 23rd @ 8:00pm; April 24th @ 6:30pm and 9:30pm; and April 25th @ 6:30pm and 9:30pm!
📍 Blackbox Theater, B2 Level West Hall - Mount Vernon Campus

Tickets will go live Tuesday, 4/21 at 8 pm: https://go.gwu.edu/fpptickets. Tickets for this event are $5 each, paid in cash or via Venmo at the door. Please arrive at least 10 minutes before the posted show time, or your presale ticket will be released to those waiting for a door ticket. 

This show contains themes of sexual harassment, adult situations, mild profanity, suggestive humor, weapons use, alcohol use, and violence.

 

Accessibility: While the West Hall Blackbox is an accessible space, the Mount Vernon Campus is partially accessible. Please reach out to fpp@gwu.edu or christopher.gagliardi@gwu.edu with any questions or concerns about accessibility & accommodations. 

 

NOTE: pre-sale is limited to 4 tickets per order.

 

Thank you for supporting Forbidden Planet Productions!

 

9 TO 5 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.mtishows.com

name: MAVAZI | 18th Annual Taste of Africa
description:
MAVAZI, meaning “clothing” in Swahili, is the 2026 edition of the African Student Association’s annual Taste of Africa showcase at The George Washington University. This year’s theme highlights the power of fashion as a form of cultural expression, storytelling, and identity across the African continent and diaspora.

Through a dynamic runway experience, MAVAZI brings together traditional and contemporary African fashion, showcasing the richness of textiles, beadwork, craftsmanship, and design. Each piece tells a story—reflecting history, heritage, and the evolving creativity of African designers and communities.

More than just a fashion show, MAVAZI is a celebration of culture, artistry, and unity. The event will feature curated looks, live performances, and an immersive atmosphere that honors the diversity and vibrancy of African cultures. Attendees can expect an evening that blends fashion, music, and storytelling into a powerful and memorable experience.

name: TEDxFoggyBottom Annual Conference 2025
description:
THIS IS A TICKETED EVENT. Head to https://www.tedxfoggybottom.org/ to purchase! 

What started in 2011 with a few students and a big idea has quickly become one of the largest student-organized TEDx events in the United States and around the world. Each year, TEDxFoggyBottom is brought to life by over 50 undergraduate students at The George Washington University in Washington, DC, who work to bring together some of the world's most incredible innovators, thinkers, and doers to inspire and collaborate with the Foggy Bottom community. We invite anyone in the DC community to join us for a day of learning, growing, and disruption. 

Tickets for the event include the ability to watch 8-10 TEDx Talks live from Betts Theater, connecting with local non-profits, a $100+ swag bag, a free catered lunch, and more.

description:
Join us for our annual end-of-year formal! Every year we celebrate our wonderful GW first-gen community and toast the graduating class. This year's theme is First Gen Oasis; think of a classy beach party mixed with White Lotus and tropical, serene vibes. At this culminating event, we'll have dinner foods, themed mocktails, and live entertainment! We'll also award two first-gen students a $500 scholarship, reminisce on the experiences of our conference participants, and surprise you with theme-based activities throughout the evening. As always, our EBoard speakers and keynote speakers will inspire you as you get ready for graduation. 

Please RSVP to ensure we have the proper headcount for food. We can't wait to see you there!

Dress/attire ideas: like you're at a resort/on vacation, tropical prints, pastel colors, white linens/breezy fabrics, summer wedding guest, khakis, or anything that makes you feel comfortable and fabulous.

Hosted at Dacha Beer Garden in Shaw, Washington, DC, the event will feature a vibrant atmosphere, great food and drinks, and the opportunity to connect with fellow members of the GW community. Whether you’re celebrating milestones, honoring achievements, or simply enjoying time with friends, this formal is the perfect way to wrap up the year.

 

Dress to impress and get ready for an unforgettable evening with the GW Student Veterans community.

name: THE ART OF MATCHA: Green Tea  & Tea Ceremony Workshop
description:
🍵 Join us for a Matcha & Japanese Tea Ceremony Workshop! 🍵

Looking for a mid-afternoon escape from finals? Step into the world of Japanese tea with JCA! We’re hosting an immersive afternoon dedicated to the art, history, and flavors of green tea.

From refreshing cold-brewed Sencha to a formal tea ceremony performance, come learn about the journey of the leaf and the traditions behind the whisk.

What’s on the menu?
✨ Tastings of Sencha, Hojicha, and Gyokuro
✨ Traditional wagashi (sweet bean snacks)
✨ A live Tea Ceremony performance
✨ Complimentary Japanese tea bags to take home!

The Details:
📅 When: Friday, April 24th
⏰ Time: 2:30 PM – 4:00 PM
📍 Where: DH B114
👥 Note: Seats are limited to 15 participants, so register early!
🔗 Registration link (also in bio!): https://forms.gle/R1qTBKVMwfduJpmb9

Whether you’re a matcha addict or just curious about Japanese culture, we can’t wait to share a cup with you. See you there in our traditional Yukata and Hakama! 👘

description: Join Partners in Health to help with fundraising for global health! There will be food and treats for sale, trivia with prizes, cotton candy, and other goodies! All proceeds go towards on-the-ground care for TB patients.

description: Join the GW Pickleball Club for open play Thursdays from 5:30-7:00 on the 3rd floor of Lerner!

name: Brain breaks & Nothing Bundt cakes: 101 to surviving finals
description: Feeling stressed about finals? Come take a break, recharge, and treat yourself! Join potomac house for a relaxing evening filled with sweet treats and simple ways to reset your mind before exams.

name: Org Help Photo Studio
description:
We’re excited to introduce our brand-new photo space! Student organization leaders are invited to stop by and capture board photos or any organization-related pictures you need. 

It’s a great opportunity to update your visuals, get creative, meet the SORC team, and explore the tools and resources available to support your organization.

name: GoodBye Madison
description: Join us for a final farewell event for Madison residents as we celebrate our last moments together as a community. This event is a chance to reflect on the memories we’ve made, connect one last time, and close out the year with appreciation and good energy. Come by, enjoy the moment, and say goodbye to Madison in a meaningful way.

name: Map Your Home
description: Add your hometown to our community map and enjoy some snacks!

name: Your Career In Marketing
description: Use the attached link to register, must use your GW email.

name: CAPS Presents: Picking Up the Pieces
description: This is a space for the many students who seek support prompted by a break-up. Navigating these break-ups and losses can be difficult for many students. The purpose of this group is to help students process and move forward through these break-up/ losses with the support of peers struggling with similar concerns.

name: Tea-rrific Finals Break
description: Take a break from finals and treat yourself! Stop by for grab-and-go boba and a curated selection of spring-inspired goodies, including cozy blankets, flower throw pillows, tote bags, faux plants, and self-care items like face masks. Refresh your space, relax for a moment, and enjoy a little seasonal pick-me-up before the end of the semester.

name: Chaplain's Corner
location: The Center for Interfaith and Spiritual Life Lounge
description:
Chaplain’s Corner: Weekly on Thursday Afternoons!
Thursdays, 3–4 PM

Take a mindful midweek break with the University Chaplain and special guests! Chaplain’s Corner offers a warm, welcoming space to relax, connect, and recharge. Enjoy coffee, tea, snacks, and good company—plus coloring pages, crafts, puzzles, and games like Uno and Connect 4. Whether you're stopping by for a few minutes or staying the whole hour, you're always welcome.

All are invited. Come as you are!

name: Acai Bar
description: Students will be able to engage with their residential community by grabbing an acai bowl and mingling with the CEA and their peers. Come stop by!

name: Study Hall
description: Join us for Study Hall! This is a great opportunity to focus, get your work done, and stay productive in a supportive environment. Whether you’re catching up on assignments or preparing for upcoming tests, take advantage of this dedicated time to succeed.

name: Pasta & Game Night
description: Come out for a night of pasta & tons of board game with your faculty in residence & CEA! Food will be provided on a first come, first served basis.

name: Movie Night
location: First Floor Community Lounge, Shenkman Hall
description: Join us for a cozy Movie Night in the community lounge with free snacks, drinks, and a film picked by residents. It’s the perfect way to relax, hang out, and take a break midweek

name: Breaking Bread: I Don't Want to be Perceived
description: This is our last Breaking Bread of the semester, and we’re ending it with a real conversation. What does it mean to be seen in a world that constantly asks us to perform? Is vulnerability something we avoid, or something we’re learning to embrace? Join us as we unpack the idea of “I Don’t Want to Be Perceived” and explore how we build authentic relationships in a time that often feels anything but real. Come ready to share, listen, reflect, and engage with others over free food and interactive activities designed to spark connection.

name: End of year celebration
description: Come get cookies, snacks, drinks and fidget toys as a end of year celebration with your CEA's

name: Can Aliens be Saved
description: Join us the Thomistic Institute for a lecture on Can Aliens be Saved. This lecture will be by Dr. Edmund Lazzari of Duquesne University at 7:30 p.m. in Duques 359.

name: BSIR Research Day
description: BSIR Research Day allows members to present reserch they've done during the school year or the previous Summer. Any student is welcome to attend and/or present, whether the project was completed with a professor, an organization, or for class. Please plan to prepare a short slideshow (or another presentation format) to share your findings. To sign-up, please fill out this Google form: https://forms.gle/cBVQhRKeDbpKDGSQ9

name: Cru Weekly Large Group

location: The Center for Interfaith and Spiritual Life Lounge
description: These sessions will explore different recitations of the Quran, the sacred text of Islam. Topics may include the social and cultural impacts of the Quran.

name: CAPS Presents: The Next Phase: a Support-Focused Group for Students Who Will Soon Graduate
description: This group is for both undergraduate and graduate school students who are nearing graduation and preparing for the next chapters in their lives. It is a peer support space where students have an opportunity to share their affective and cognitive experiences regarding their futures. This mutual disclosure and exploration is intended to help normalize the students' experiences and facilitate support, encouragement and helpful reflection and feedback.

description:
Start your morning right with Bagel 4 Breakfast 🥯

 

Join us in the South Lobby Lounge on Wednesday, April 22 at 10 AM for fresh bagels and a quick bite before your day gets going. Swing by early—food is available until it runs out!

name: Panera Fundraiser
description: Join us for a delicious way to give back! We’re partnering with Panera Bread for a special fundraiser where a portion of all sales will support our cause. Stop by, enjoy your favorite soups, salads, sandwiches, and baked goods, and help make a difference in our community. Whether you dine in, take out, or order online (using our fundraiser code, if applicable), every purchase counts. Bring your friends and family—great food tastes even better when it’s for a good cause!
